title: Gesture-based cueing experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad exploring 'gesture-based' cueing: tiny, explicit editorial gestures in prompts (short patterns, punctuation, line breaks, invisible separators) to nudge models into different response shapes without heavy instructions or long exemplars. Goal is to find compact primitives that are robust across model families and tokenization quirks.

Motivation notes:
- Long few-shot contexts are expensive; can we get stable stylistic/structural control with <40 token cues?
- Observed brittle behavior when cues are lexically similar to dataset artifacts. Need orthogonal gestures.
- Useful for embedding into product templates (UI placeholders, ephemeral system messages).

Hypothesis clusters:
1) Visual separators (e.g., ◆, --- , :::) act as structural anchors for lists and headings.
2) Micro-prefaces (single-word gesture like "Sketchy:") bias tone without imposing constraints.
3) Invisible tokens (zero-width space sequences) break token alignment and sometimes force paraphrase — risky across quantized models.

Quick experiment matrix (stateful):
- Models: redwood-1-small, open-rl-7b, community-13b-quant
- Cues: [":::", "—", "◆", "Sketchy:", "Brief:", "\u200B\u200B"]
- Tasks: summarization (3-sentence), bullet extraction, code comment generation
- Metric: structural fidelity (human), token delta, repetition rate, hallucination notes

Sample templates (iterating):
1) Minimal list extractor
Prompt: "Input:
{{TEXT}}
:::
Return only 1-5 concise bullets with no commentary."
Notes: good on redwood-1-small when cue is ":::"; open-rl sometimes emits preamble.

2) Tone micro-preface
Prompt: "Tone: Sketchy
Task: Explain in plain terms why cache hits matter."
Notes: "Sketchy" tends to produce casual phrasing on community-13b but occasionally omits key details.

3) Invisible-break paraphrase
Prompt: "Rewrite:{{TEXT}}
\u200B\u200B Paraphrase concisely."
Notes: community-13b-quant splits tokens oddly; results sometimes shorter but with hallucinated facts. Avoid for factual-sensitive tasks.

Observed failure cases (catalog):
- Cue hijacking: when input text contains the cue token (e.g., input already has ":::") model treats it as part of content. Mitigation: randomized cue variants per request.
- Overfitting to micro-preface literalness: some gestures get appended back in the response (e.g., "Sketchy:" appears in output). Postprocess strip needed.
- Quantization sensitivity: invisible token strategies amplify hallucinations in quantized checkpoints.

Small reproducible examples (copyable):
- EX1: Summarize (redwood-1-small)
Input: long blog paragraph about KV caching
Prompt: "Blog:
{{blog}}
---
Summarize in 2 bullets."
Observed: consistent 2 bullets, but sometimes a third short fragment on open-rl.

- EX2: Code comment generation (community-13b-quant)
Prompt: "Function:
{{fn}}
◆
Add concise comment at top describing purpose and complexity."
Observed: good for single-file functions; fails when fn contains docstrings with similar markers.

Instrumentation ideas:
- Tag each request with chosen cue and record: output length, top-token entropy, fails/strip-needed boolean.
- A/B deploy cue variants behind feature flag to collect signal for dedicated customers.

Next experiments (short backlog):
- 1) Randomized cue set per model family to detect cue collision rate (ticket attached).
- 2) Build micro-benchmark of 120 inputs across summarization/code/commenting and run nightly to track drift.
- 3) Test combos: cue + micro-preface (e.g., "Brief: :::") to see additive effects.

Edge ethics / safety notes:
- Because cues are small surface-level edits, they can be abused to subtly change instruction adherence. When used in customer-facing automation, include explicit audit fields recording the gesture used.

TODOs (personal):
- Clean-up: canonicalize a 6-cue whitelist for product templates.
- Write up short note for DE team with sample failures and suggested postprocess strips.
- Pair with Arjun to prototype telemetry labels (cue_id, cue_variant).

Links and references:
- Linear ticket: ISSUE-482 for randomized cue rollout.
- Draft PR: prompt-lab/pulls/187 contains small harness for inserting separators.

Quick log:
2025-06-17 created initial idea
2025-08-02 first micro-benchmark run (n=40) shows separator signal strong for bullet tasks
2025-12-11 found invisible-token bug on quantized 13b
2026-02-28 consolidated notes and cleaned sample templates

Notes to self (messy):
- avoid zero-width for anything that feeds downstream extractors
- prefer visible glyphs with low lexical overlap with typical corpora (◆, ▸, —)
- canonicalize removal regex to avoid deleting legitimate hyphenation

End of scratchpad.
